RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel may violate university guidelines on panel composition, and subtle affinity or homophily bias can occur in academic hiring. However, composition alone does not prove discrimination. Selection panels frequently weigh criteria beyond publication counts, such as interview execution, teaching demonstrations, subfield fit, or industry experience tailored to specific curriculum needs.

Avoid leading with direct accusations of sex bias, which can harm professional relationships without concrete proof. Instead, review the university’s published hiring and equity policies regarding panel composition. Send a polite follow-up requesting your written feedback and scoring rubric, and consult human resources or a staff union representative to determine whether standard procedural guidelines were followed.
